numeric_prose_changes.old: Within each 252-session training window, a 60-session rolling standard deviation is computed for each asset. The latest cross-asset average volatility is compared with the median of the cross-asset averages available inside that same training window. Tau is 0.01 when the latest value exceeds that median and 0.05 otherwise. Only prior observations enter the decision. A smaller tau gives less weight to the historical tilt relative to the prior in this construction. The rule was not selected in Phase 4 to improve performance.

numeric_prose_changes.old: Table 7 and Figure 7 present Phase 1's US four-factor diagnostic. Market beta is 1.063528 for BL and 1.148195 for Markowitz. No direct cross-strategy test of beta equality is supplied, so the estimates are not called statistically indistinguishable. The US BL SMB coefficient is positive and its HML coefficient is positive in the retained fit; the Markowitz size loading is negative, while its HML coefficient has substantial statistical uncertainty. Full coefficients and HAC inference are reported rather than inferring their signs from a figure alone.
